Class AIRequestLimiter

java.lang.Object
limits.AIRequestLimiter
public class AIRequestLimiter extends Object

Title: AIRequestLimiter Class

Description: This class limits how many AI requests each user can make. It is a prototype for TP3 Aspect #2, "Staff actions have limits" (CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits). Every AI feature in TP3 (curator AI search terms, curator AI editing, and the contributor AI writing tools) asks this class before sending a request, so one user can't use up the AI tools for everyone, and the free-tier limits of the AI services (LanguageTool and Grammarly, from our AICoaching.pdf) aren't reached.

Each user can make at most DEFAULT_MAX_REQUESTS requests in any 60-minute period (Initial ConOps.pdf, objective O1). A request stops counting once it is 60 minutes old. When the limit is reached, the user gets a message saying how many minutes until they can try again (objective O6).

Like the PasswordEvaluator class, tryRequest returns an empty String when the request is allowed, or the message the GUI should show.

  • Method Details

    • tryRequest

      public String tryRequest(String userName, long nowMillis)

      Method: String tryRequest(String userName, long nowMillis)

      Description: Asks to make one AI request. If the user is under the limit, the request is recorded and "" is returned, so the AI feature can go ahead. If they are at the limit, nothing is recorded and a message is returned.

      Parameters:
      userName - is the logged-in user making the request
      nowMillis - is the current time in milliseconds (System.currentTimeMillis() in the app; a fixed time in the tests)
      Returns:
      "" if the request is allowed, else the message to show the user

    • getRemaining

      public int getRemaining(String userName, long nowMillis)

      Method: int getRemaining(String userName, long nowMillis)

      Description: Tells how many requests the user has left right now, so a page can show something like "AI requests left this hour: 12".

      Parameters:
      userName - is the logged-in user
      nowMillis - is the current time in milliseconds
      Returns:
      the number of requests left, or 0 if there is no logged-in user

    • timesFor

      private Deque<Long> timesFor(String userName)

      Method: Deque<Long> timesFor(String userName)

      Description: Gets the request times for one user, creating an empty list the first time the user makes a request. Keeping a separate list per user is what keeps one user from blocking everyone else (A4).

      Parameters:
      userName - is the user
      Returns:
      that user's request times, oldest first

    • removeExpired

      private void removeExpired(Deque<Long> times, long nowMillis)

      Method: void removeExpired(Deque<Long> times, long nowMillis)

      Description: Removes the requests that are 60 minutes old or older, since they no longer count.

      Parameters:

    • minutesUntilFree

      private String minutesUntilFree(Deque<Long> times, long nowMillis)

      Method: String minutesUntilFree(Deque<Long> times, long nowMillis)

      Description: Works out how long until the user's oldest request expires, as text for the message, for example "40 minutes" or "1 minute".

      Parameters:
      times - is one user's request times, oldest first (not empty)
      nowMillis - is the current time in milliseconds
      Returns:
      the wait time as text
